summary: Careful, well-instrumented preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-in-the-loop (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration generation. Execution and artifact records are comprehensive; the run completed as preregistered but produced a degenerate null (baseline and guarded both passed the forbidden-reachability predicate for all N=300 pairs, so the GVR repair path was never exercised). The manuscript correctly interprets limits of this outcome and archives reproducibility artifacts, but a few audit- and reporting-level defects must be corrected before finalisation.
critical_issues: The analysis used 10,000 bootstrap resamples even though the preregistration planned 1,000; this deviation is not recorded in the preregistration/deviation fields and is not documented in the manuscript (deviation-from-preregistration not disclosed).

Validator provenance and configuration are insufficiently specified in the manuscript: the text names a containerized Batfish and a Python static analyzer but does not state explicit software versions, key configuration options, or the exact decision rule(s) used by each verifier (these details appear present in the archived artifacts but are not cited or summarized in the paper).

The manuscript includes heavy provenance and artifact-inventory wording in the main text (numerous artifact paths/hashes). This reads partly like an artifact log rather than concise scholarly prose; essential provenance should be retained but long inventories should be moved to the evidence bundle and replaced by succinct references in the main paper.
required_revisions: Add an explicit, machine-readable and human-readable deviation disclosure stating that bootstrap_resamples was increased from the preregistered 1,000 to 10,000, provide the artifact path(s) (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) that show this, and briefly justify the change (deterministic/computational reason). This must be recorded both in the execution/analysis manifest and described in the Methods/Analysis paragraph of the manuscript.

Add explicit verifier provenance and configuration statements in the Methods (one short paragraph): provide Batfish container image identifier/version and the key Batfish analyses/configuration used (policy/reachability checks), and provide the Python static analyzer implementation identifier/version and its decision rule (artifact paths and hashes are acceptable references). If these exact strings live in the archived artifacts, cite those artifact paths and their SHA-256 hashes in the manuscript.

Replace lengthy in-text artifact inventories with concise pointers: move detailed file-path and hash listings to the evidence bundle and in the manuscript include a single short sentence pointing readers to the evidence bundle (give the manifest file path and representative hash). Keep only essential provenance statements in the paper (e.g., which validators were used, that all raw traces are archived) and remove repeated per-file listings that occupy narrative space.
optional_revisions: In Discussion, add a brief explicit paragraph summarizing how the shared_initial_generation contract (one shared LLM draw per pair) affected the ability to exercise the repair path, and point to the execution manifest entries that record 'shared_initial_generation' = 300 (already present in artifacts).

Consider adding a short table (1 paragraph or compact block) summarizing task difficulty distribution and representative task families (these summaries are available in execution/task_manifest.jsonl) to help readers assess external validity and difficulty mix.
Cite exact Batfish and Python analyzer license/URL or repository commit in the references if available in the archived evidence bundle; this will help readers reuse the verifier implementations.
